text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London gave up all of their gains and dipped into negative territory by the close as fund selling in New York pressured the market. August lost $1.90 to close at $312.50, while October gave up $3.70 to close at $303.10. Raw sugar futures in New York closed lower across the board with front month May losing 7 points to close at 11.46 cents/lb, while July gave up 17 points to close at 11.07 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 7 and 11 points. Although Russia has been an active buyer of raw sugar recently, physical demand in general remains slack. Physical sugar brokers reported little activity in the second-hand raws market as Brazil's new crop has yet to come on stream and Cuba holds back cargoes in the hope of better prices.

CHINA - China imported 24,055 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in March 1996, down from the 64,288 tonnes imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996/97 (September) up to 483,000 tonnes, significantly down from last year's figure of 1.234 million tonnes and 1994/95 imports of 1.425 million tonnes. Exports in March 1996 reached 20,800 tonnes while no sugar was exported the same month the previous year. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1996/97 up to 201,000 tonnes which compares to 578,000 tonnes the same period in 1995/96 and 472,000 tonnes in 1994/95. The import figures for the first seven months of 1996/97 indicate that earlier expectations for the crop year may have to be scaled down.

UKRAINE - Even though it had been reported that cold weather has delayed sugar beet sowings the ministry of agriculture now said that 163,000 ha have been sown with sugar beet at the end of April against 9,000 ha at this time in 1996. Given subsequent favourable weather sugar beet sowings should be completed earlier than last year, which would lengthen the vegetation period and could lead to higher yields.

YUGOSLAVIA - Damage to the 1997/98 sugar crop due to frost seems to be more severe than initially expected. According to industry sources, frost destroyed beets on 15,000 to 20,000 ha compared to 10,000 ha reported previously. Although beets were resown on 12,000 ha it is not yet clear what the final damage will be. The late sowings will reduce the growing period by a month or so. The total area sown to beet in the end will range between 50,000 and 60,000 ha, down from 70,000 ha in 1996 and also considerably below the government's target of 100,000 ha.

SINGAPORE - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 31,011 tonnes, raw value, up from 29,501 tonnes in December 1995. This brought total imports in 1996 up to record highs of 313,726 tonnes against 271,334 tonnes in 1995 and 285,420 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in calendar year 1996 were Australia with 80,001 tonnes raws against 174,014 tonnes, Thailand with 80,000 tonnes, up from 8,040 tonnes and Malaysia with 63,282 tonnes whites compared to 52,896 tonnes. Sugar exports in calendar year 1996 amounted to 11,148 tonnes, down from 22,136 tonnes in 1995. The major country of destination in 1996 was Brunei with 2,277 tonnes against 1,761 tonnes in 1995.

SWEDEN - Sugar exports in January 1997 amounted to 4,115 tonnes, raw value, up from 1,139 tonnes in January 1996. This brought cumulative exports in the first five months of 1996/97 (September/January) up to 17,330 tonnes against 12,111 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 32,576 tonnes against 17,610 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in September/January 1996/97 were Norway with 6,887 tonnes whites against 97 tonnes and Estonia with 3,801 tonnes, up from 1,000.
